problem: Repository CI and build inputs rely on third-party code/artifacts while existing application-security and CI-reliability skills deliberately do not own dependency/action/artifact provenance and integrity.
triggers: third-party CI action or plugin refs
build provenance or SBOM trust review
overlap_review: application-security-local-first owns runtime/application security; ci-pipeline-reliability owns whether integrity gates execute; provenance-contract tracks repository source attribution/license evidence. This skill owns technical identity/integrity/provenance of software inputs and artifacts.
current_evidence: Phases 11 and 13 expose the problem class before this skill existed. No controlled post-creation behavioral execution has tested whether loading software-supply-chain-integrity improves review outcomes.

minimum_criteria: mutable/unverified third-party executable input is identified
version pinning is separated from integrity/provenance evidence
critical artifact/input receives an explicit verification mechanism and trust boundary
result does not claim application security or release safety

limitations: integrity/provenance does not prove absence of vulnerabilities or malicious logic
trust depends on signer/builder/source identity and policy
lockfiles and SBOMs are not complete security proofs
promotion_requirements: execute at least one controlled post-creation supply-chain review case
show criterion-level value beyond application-security and CI guidance
rejection_condition: Retire or fold into security/CI guidance if real use shows supply-chain integrity is not independently useful.
